subject.title: max for live devices
subject.subtitle: user guide
subject.blurb: An aide-mémoire for the devices in the Max for Live folder — what every control does, how the Push 3 encoders are laid out, and the handful of things each one needs you to remember.

items.name: Cascade
items.tagline: Multi-tap machine — up to 64 echoes spread across a window you shape by hand.

items.name: Microcosmos
items.tagline: Replica of the Hologram Microcosm pedal — 11 granular / loop effects, 44 variations, and a 30-second phrase looper.

items.name: Pulsograph
items.tagline: Early-electronic rhythm machine — four synthesis lanes on a 32-step grid that drifts like a real motor.

items.name: ORAM
items.tagline: Drawn sound after Daphne Oram's Oramics — paint film strips and the machine performs them.

items.name: The 1958 Machine
items.tagline: Turns anything into the sound of the early European electronic-music studios, c. 1950–65.

items.name: Splice (Tape Collage)
items.tagline: A 1950s random tape editor — razor-blades your recordings and splices them back together, imperfections included.

items.name: Ondes Martenot
items.tagline: Monophonic MPE Ondes voice for Push 3 pads — pressure is the envelope.

items.name: SW Radio
items.tagline: Tunes a KiwiSDR shortwave receiver anywhere in the world from inside Live.

items.name: YT Sampler
items.tagline: Paste a YouTube link, bracket a phrase, drop it into Session view as a clip.

items.name: Preset Scroll
items.tagline: Scroll an Arturia plugin's preset browser from a Push encoder.

items.name: Manual Tape
items.tagline: Hand-controlled sample playback — a tape reel you push forwards and backwards by hand.

items.name: Scene Placer
items.tagline: Places a voice or source inside a loaded environment recording.

items.name: False Memory
items.tagline: Degradation effect — parallel analog and digital damage paths under one intensity macro.

items.name: Tape Error
items.tagline: Fire a tape fault on an audio track from a note on a MIDI track — velocity is severity.

items.name: Strip Silence
items.tagline: Removes the silence from arrangement recordings — non-destructive clip trimming, one undo step.

items.name: Disintegration
items.tagline: Cumulative tape-oxide loss — one reel, deterministic damage, 256 passes.

items.name: Magnabelt
items.tagline: Spiral-belt sampler after Holger Czukay's IBM dictaphone — one wandering head, adjacent passes, imperfect erasure.

items.name: Evening Star
items.tagline: Frippertronics twin tape-loop system — two machine pairs that build slow soundscapes, darken with every pass and ebb away on command.
